Most common skill I use day-to-day with LLMs is a summary technique I term 3-stepping.

I invoke it like this in both Claude & ChatGPT:

3step <link>

It outputs a 3-layered summary. Layer 1 is a one paragraph concise summary, Layer 2 is a two paragraph deeper overview of interesting details, Layer 3 is a three paragraph full analysis / critique.

I find it much more helpful than just an LLM to "summarize X." Most things I just read layer 1, but it allows me to decide how deep into any particular link I want to go. And if I get through all 3 layers and find it interesting enough, I'll read the original.

If you want my read on current landscape:

-> Chinese pluggable makers like CIG (剑桥科技) are facing severe shortages in 70mW-200mW lasers.

If you look at filings from CIG, they claim "substantially longer delivery times and deposits to secure capacity” along with statements of shortages.

-> Innolight and others were also looking to secure multiple laser suppliers with LTAs recently from their filings. 

On the US side of things:

-> $COHR was a major merchant laser supplier before, but largely withdrew from the market after rerouting them internally. 

"I do not see any time in the near future where we would be selling Indium Phosphide lasers externally." From their ER transcript. 

And then likely turned into a buyer in an already supply constrained market... where 

"over the long term, we will have some portion of our datacom transceivers that will be supported by external sources."

-> $AAOI not really known to be a merchant supplier, but said same thing about laser capacity being rerouted towards transceivers. And having to turn away customers for lasers. 

-> For $LITE, they still supply lasers but stated: "We are commanding a significant price premium" for CW lasers

$LITE Wupen Yuen: "wherever they can get the laser source, they will use that solution to support their build-out."

So hinting... about customers just finding anything available due to shortages. 

-> $MTSI has no meaningful capacity online now, but they're already stating customers are approaching them with urgency to secure CW laser supply. 

-> Trendforce reported $AMD and hyperscaler CSPs are aggressively going out to secure CW laser supply to avoid future bottlenecks. 

And then you have Europe... 

Where $SIVE is coming online with "tremendous capacity available now" from their foundry partners. 

With 100M+ laser capacity Q4 2027, and maybe if you look at their 2:1 ratio implying ~200M targeted laser capacity from external foundries. 

They also happen to offer the same power range (70mW, 100 mW, 200mW) as the ones currently in shortage by pluggable makers in China. 

There's a massive void to fill, so this dramatically increases the chance of converting customers. (esp. Supported by Lumentum statements)

My speculation was that some of the 6 active pluggable engagements were from China? 

Which is why they're attending the conference.

- if Europe is a laser source geography, if Innolight/Eoptolink/Cambridge are considering $SIVE. 
- if they're seeing ASP hikes in lasers, and what CW products are hardest to obtain

If you are attending CIOE in Shenzhen!

Very few people will actually notice the step change from GPT 5.6 to GPT 6 Astra. The reason is simple: most everyday tasks are already saturated. AI is already at 100%.

I can ask ChatGPT to find the email of a babysitter, email her, send a calendar invite, then text my wife. Or take a photo of my bike tire, have it identify the exact tire, research it, and tell me the right PSI.

It already does all of this extremely well. There is no 120%.So if I switch to Astra, I may see almost 0 difference. Maybe it is faster and cheaper, but with a subscription you barely feel either.

The capability jump will be obvious if you are at the frontier of coding, math or science. For everyone else, AI has become so good that the next huge leap might feel surprisingly invisible.
